words.definition: Correct. Matching the facts.
words.example: Is it true that you're moving?

words.definition: Not true; wrong.
words.example: That's a false alarm.

words.definition: Existing, not imaginary or fake.
words.example: Is that a real diamond?

words.definition: Completely sure, or definite.
words.example: I'm certain I locked the door.

words.definition: Confident that something is true.
words.example: Are you sure you want to go?

words.definition: Easy to see or understand.
words.example: The answer is obvious.

words.definition: Easy to understand, see or hear.
words.example: The instructions weren't clear.

words.definition: Correct and exact.
words.example: Is this map accurate?

words.definition: Right; without mistakes.
words.example: Your answer is correct.

words.definition: Able to happen or be done.
words.example: Is it possible to change my seat?

words.definition: To make your muscles longer by reaching or pulling.
words.example: Stretch before you run.

words.definition: The food you usually eat, or a special plan for eating less.
words.example: A healthy diet includes lots of vegetables.

words.definition: How heavy something or someone is.
words.example: He lost a lot of weight last year.

words.definition: A part of the body that helps you move.
words.example: I pulled a muscle in my back.

words.definition: To produce water through your skin when you are hot.
words.example: I sweat a lot when I run.

words.definition: To take air into your lungs and let it out.
words.example: Breathe in slowly and count to four.

words.definition: The strength you need to do things.
words.example: I have no energy today.

words.definition: A feeling of worry caused by problems or pressure.
words.example: Exercise helps me deal with stress.

words.definition: Something you do regularly, often without thinking.
words.example: Drinking water in the morning is a good habit.

words.definition: To become healthy again, like a cut or a broken bone.
words.example: It takes weeks for a broken arm to heal.

words.definition: To send air out of your mouth, or to move as the wind does.
words.example: Blow out the candles and make a wish.

words.definition: To be damaged by fire or heat, or to destroy with fire.
words.example: Careful, you'll burn the toast.

words.definition: To bite food many times before swallowing.
words.example: Chew your food slowly.

words.definition: To hit your hands together to show you like something.
words.example: The audience clapped loudly.

words.definition: To hit something hard, or when a computer stops working suddenly.
words.example: My laptop crashed during the meeting.

words.definition: To break into small pieces.
words.example: The old wall started to crumble.

words.definition: To be brave enough to do something.
words.example: I wouldn't dare to ask him.

words.definition: To handle something or someone. Often "deal with".
words.example: How do you deal with stress?

words.definition: To think that something will happen.
words.example: I didn't expect so many people to come.

words.definition: To be real or to be alive.
words.example: Do you think ghosts really exist?

words.definition: A tool for hitting nails.
words.example: Hand me the hammer, please.

words.definition: A tool for turning screws.
words.example: I need a screwdriver to fix this chair.

words.definition: A set of steps you climb to reach high places.
words.example: Hold the ladder while I climb up.

words.definition: A thick, strong cord.
words.example: Tie the boat with a strong rope.

words.definition: A round open container with a handle, for carrying liquids.
words.example: Fill the bucket with water.

words.definition: A thin metal thread, often used to carry electricity.
words.example: A loose wire made the lamp stop working.

words.definition: The glass part of a lamp that gives light.
words.example: The bulb in the hallway burned out.

words.definition: A thin metal pin that you hit into wood.
words.example: I need a nail to hang this picture.

words.definition: An object you hold to do a particular job.
words.example: Do you have the right tool for this job?

words.definition: A sticky substance used to join things.
words.example: I'll fix the handle with some glue.

words.definition: The meat from a cow.
words.example: I'd like the beef stew.

words.definition: The meat from a pig.
words.example: We had roast pork for dinner.

words.definition: The meat from a young sheep.
words.example: He ordered a lamb chop.

words.definition: Salted pork cut in thin slices.
words.example: I love bacon and eggs.

words.definition: A tube of chopped meat and spices.
words.example: We grilled sausages at the barbecue.

words.definition: A thick slice of meat, usually beef.
words.example: How would you like your steak cooked?

words.definition: A small sea animal with a curved body, eaten as food.
words.example: I'll have the garlic shrimp.

words.definition: A large pink fish.
words.example: Grilled salmon is my favorite.

words.definition: A large sea fish, often sold in cans.
words.example: I made a tuna sandwich.

words.definition: Salted or smoked meat from a pig's leg.
words.example: Can I have a ham and cheese sandwich?

words.definition: To look at things to see how they are alike or different.
words.example: Let's compare prices before we buy.

words.definition: Almost the same, but not exactly.
words.example: Our phones are very similar.

words.definition: Not the same.
words.example: This one is different from the one I ordered.

words.definition: Exactly alike, not different.
words.example: We have the same birthday.

words.definition: The same in size, amount or value.
words.example: Cut the cake into equal pieces.

words.definition: A way in which things are not the same.
words.example: What's the difference between these two?

words.definition: One or the other of two.
words.example: You can take either road. Both go to the beach.

words.definition: Not one and not the other.
words.example: Neither of us wanted to cook.

words.definition: Preferably. Used in "would rather" to say what you prefer.
words.example: I'd rather stay in tonight.

words.definition: In place of something else.
words.example: We were going to drive, but we took the train instead.

words.definition: One of the five long parts at the end of your hand.
words.example: I cut my finger with a knife.

words.definition: The short, thick finger on the side of your hand.
words.example: He gave me a thumbs up.

words.definition: One of the five small parts at the end of your foot.
words.example: I hurt my toe.

words.definition: Your hand closed tightly.
words.example: He clenched his fist.

words.definition: The inside part of your hand.
words.example: She held the coin in her palm.

words.definition: One of the two soft edges of your mouth.
words.example: She bit her lip.

words.definition: The soft part of your face below your eye.
words.example: He kissed her on the cheek.

words.definition: The part of your body between your chest and hips.
words.example: She tied a belt around her waist.

words.definition: The part at the side of your body where your leg meets your body.
words.example: She put her hands on her hips.

words.definition: The joint between your hand and arm.
words.example: I sprained my wrist.

words.definition: The largest city in South Africa.
words.example: Johannesburg is big.

words.definition: A city in Morocco.
words.example: Casablanca is a port.

words.definition: The capital of Iran.
words.example: Tehran is crowded.

words.definition: The capital of Iraq.
words.example: Baghdad is on the Tigris.

words.definition: An ancient city in Israel.
words.example: Jerusalem is holy to many.

words.definition: The capital of Saudi Arabia.
words.example: Riyadh is in the desert.

words.definition: A large city in Pakistan.
words.example: Karachi is on the coast.

words.definition: A city in Pakistan.
words.example: Lahore has great food.

words.definition: A city in India.
words.example: Kolkata is known for culture.

words.definition: A technology city in India.
words.example: Bangalore has many tech companies.

words.definition: A set of rooms for living in, in a larger building.
words.example: We're looking for a bigger apartment.

words.definition: A person who owns a home and rents it to others.
words.example: I called my landlord about the broken heater.

words.definition: A person who pays rent to use a home.
words.example: The new tenant moves in on Monday.

words.definition: Things like tables, chairs and beds in a home.
words.example: We bought all our furniture secondhand.

words.definition: Money you pay first to keep something or to protect the owner.
words.example: I paid a deposit of one month's rent.

words.definition: A legal agreement to rent a property for a period of time.
words.example: My lease ends in June.

words.definition: A machine that carries people up and down in a building.
words.example: The elevator is broken, so we took the stairs.

words.definition: A small platform outside an upstairs window.
words.example: We have breakfast on the balcony in summer.

words.definition: The top outside part of a building.
words.example: The roof leaks when it rains.

words.definition: A room or floor below ground level.
words.example: The washing machine is in the basement.

words.definition: A hard, shiny material like iron or copper.
words.example: The gate is made of metal.

words.definition: A valuable yellow metal.
words.example: She wears a thin gold ring.

words.definition: A shiny, gray-white metal.
words.example: My grandmother has a silver spoon collection.

words.definition: A strong metal made from iron.
words.example: The bridge is made of steel.

words.definition: A soft cloth made from the cotton plant.
words.example: I prefer cotton T-shirts in summer.

words.definition: The soft hair of sheep, used to make clothes.
words.example: This wool sweater keeps me warm.

words.definition: A smooth, soft cloth made by silkworms.
words.example: She bought a silk scarf in Thailand.

words.definition: A stretchy material used for tires and boots.
words.example: You need rubber boots in this weather.

words.definition: A hard natural material used for building, or a small piece of rock.
words.example: The old church is built of stone.

words.definition: Tiny pieces of rock that cover beaches and deserts.
words.example: The kids built a castle in the sand.
